stem:
Arjun watches the night sky from his rooftop in Jaipur for three hours. He notices that the Pole Star (Dhruva Tara) stays in almost the same position, while other stars seem to move around it.

Why does the Pole Star appear nearly stationary?

options.text: The Pole Star does not move at all in space
Earth's rotation axis points very close to the Pole Star
The other stars pull the Pole Star towards them
The Pole Star is the brightest star in the night sky

teacher.key_rationale: The Pole Star appears nearly stationary because Earth's rotation axis points very close to it; Earth's rotation makes the other stars appear to trace circles around it. Option A is the trap for students who swap the correct reason for the sibling claim that the star itself never moves; C and D are plausible but irrelevant surface features.
